questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize a particular element using 'it' + 'be'.
questions.question: It was ___ that secured his victory.

questions.def: 'Much as' introduces a concession with emphasis.
questions.question: ___ I appreciate your offer, I must decline.

questions.def: Negative adverbials invert subject/auxiliary: 'Never have I seen...'
questions.question: Never I have seen such beauty.

questions.def: 'Did + verb' adds emphasis to a statement.
questions.question: He ___ ever having met her.

questions.def: 'Try as' creates emphatic concession.
questions.question: ___ hard she tried, she couldn't succeed.

questions.def: Cleft sentences use 'it is' + noun phrase for emphasis.
questions.question: It is ___ that bothers me.

questions.def: 'Only after' requires inversion: 'Only after had I...'
questions.question: Only after I had left I realised my mistake.

questions.def: 'Little' requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Little ___ that danger awaited.

questions.def: 'Not only...but also' requires 'not only' at the start.
questions.question: Not ___ did he apologize, but he also offered compensation.

questions.def: 'Strange as it may seem' is an emphatic inversion.
questions.question: ___ as it may seem, it's true.

questions.def: 'So + adjective' needs subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: So important the issue was that the meeting lasted hours.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Only then ___ the gravity of the situation.

questions.def: 'Be that as it may' is an emphatic concessive phrase.
questions.question: ___ be that as it may, we must proceed.

questions.def: Cleft sentences can use pronouns emphatically: 'It is he...'
questions.question: It ___ who is responsible.

questions.def: 'Rarely' requires subject-auxiliary inversion: 'Rarely have I...'
questions.question: Rarely I have witnessed such dedication to a cause.

questions.def: 'Do' + verb emphasizes desire.
questions.question: What I ___ is a little peace and quiet.

questions.def: 'Come what may' is an emphatic expression of determination.
questions.question: Come ___ may, I will finish this project.

questions.def: 'Much as' introduces a contrasting idea emphatically.
questions.question: ___ I disagree with you, I respect your opinion.

questions.def: 'No sooner had' requires inversion: 'No sooner had the bell...'
questions.question: No sooner the bell had rung than the students left.

questions.def: 'No matter how' is an emphatic expression.
questions.question: No ___ how difficult, I will succeed.

questions.def: 'Such...that' expresses a high degree of something.
questions.question: ___ was his dedication that he worked day and night.

questions.def: Cleft sentences use 'it is' + that-clause for emphasis.
questions.question: It ___ that she needs to relax.

questions.def: 'Seldom' requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Seldom she had experienced such kindness from strangers.

questions.def: Subjunctive mood after 'recommend'.
questions.question: I do recommend that he ___ the offer.

questions.def: 'Whatever the consequence' is emphatic.
questions.question: ___ the consequence, he would act.

questions.def: Cleft sentences can use pronouns emphatically: 'It is they...'
questions.question: It ___ who must take responsibility.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires inversion.
questions.question: Under no circumstances I will accept such behaviour.

questions.def: 'Do' + verb emphasizes importance.
questions.question: What I ___ is the importance of education.

questions.def: 'Even if' emphasizes a condition.
questions.question: ___ if it rains, we will proceed with the event.

questions.def: Cleft sentences use 'it was' + noun phrase for emphasis.
questions.question: It ___ their lack of preparation that caused the failure.
